21 Sep 2022 • [Mitchell Trousers](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com/category/our-patterns/mitchell-trousers/) • by [Heather Lou](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com//author/closetcasefilesgmail-com)

# Introducing the Mitchell Trousers!

![Mitchell-Trousers-Pattern_Pants-Pattern-5](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Mitchell-Trousers-Pattern_Pants-Pattern-5.jpg)

After consecutive [lingerie(opens in new tab)](https://closetcorepatterns.com/collections/sewing-patterns-all/products/chez-moi-collection-bundle?variant=39712032686214) and [swim(opens in new tab)](https://closetcorepatterns.com/collections/sewing-patterns-all/products/faye-swimsuit-pattern?variant=39778960965766) pattern launches this year, it feels SO GOOD to finally introduce some new woven clothing patterns back into the CCP family! We couldn't be happier to add the [Mitchell Trousers](https://closetcorepatterns.com/products/mitchell-trousers-pattern) to our roster, destined to be a wardrobe staple for you this fall and beyond.

Mitchell is our take on a classic pleated trouser. These are too perennial to ever \*really\* go out of style, but if you follow fashion, you've surely noticed trousers are back in a very big way (no doubt a reaction to all the sweats we've been wearing the last few years!) Last fall I was desperate for an alternative to elastic waist pants, so we developed Mitchell to scratch that particular itch. I'm a bit obsessed with the final design - they look super sophisticated and pulled together while also being very comfortable to wear all day long.

![](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com//wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Mitchell-Trousers-Pattern_Plus-Size-Pants-Pattern-09.jpg)![](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com//wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Mitchell-Trousers-Pattern_Pants-Pattern-3.jpg)

[Mitchell](https://closetcorepatterns.com/products/mitchell-trousers-pattern) is a unique trouser pattern in that it doesn't have a waistband. High-waisted and designed to sit at your natural waist, you get a sleek, continuous line throughout the rise. The waist itself is stabilized with an inner facing, so it has all the structure of a waistband without the discomfort of one digging into your middle. We also wanted to avoid the volume around the midsection that can result from too many pleats, so instead, we have one deep pleat that provides sitting ease and comfort while also looking rather architectural and cool as it integrates into the front angled pocket. The pleat is anchored for the first few inches, so again, you don't get that tummy volume you might be used to from traditional pleated pants.

[SHOP MITCHELL(opens in new tab)](https://closetcorepatterns.com/products/mitchell-trousers-pattern)

![](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com//wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Mitchell-Trousers-Pattern_Pants-Pattern-8.jpg)

We love giving you bang for your buck, so we drafted two different major variations for this pattern: a wide leg with a floor-skimming deep hem, and a tapered, slightly cropped leg. This gives you lots of styling and shoe options, whether you want to wear them long with a heel, or cropped and tapered with an oxford, flat, or sneaker.

![](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com//wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Mitchell-Trousers-Pattern_Pants-Pattern-7.jpg)![](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com//wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Mitchell-Trousers-Pattern_Pants-Pattern-9.jpg)![](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com//wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Mitchell-Trousers-Pattern_Plus-Size-Pants-Pattern-01.jpg)![](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com//wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Mitchell-Trousers-Pattern_Plus-Size-Pants-Pattern-04.jpg)![](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com//wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Mitchell-Trousers-Pattern_Plus-Size-Pants-Pattern-06.jpg)![](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com//wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Mitchell-Trousers-Pattern_Plus-Size-Pants-Pattern-08.jpg)![](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com//wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Mitchell-Trousers-Pattern_Pants-Pattern-1.jpg)![](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com//wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Mitchell-Trousers-Pattern_Pants-Pattern-4.jpg)

_Fabrics we used: [Cream recycled denim(opens in new tab)](https://corefabricstore.com/collections/bottomweight/products/upcycled-midweight-10-5-oz-denim-cream), [lightweight denim(opens in new tab)](https://corefabricstore.com/collections/denim-twill/products/6-75-oz-non-stretch-denim-shirting-slate-blue), [yellow textured cotton(opens in new tab)](https://corefabricstore.com/collections/bottomweight/products/textured-non-stretch-cotton-honey), [deadstock wool. (opens in new tab)](https://corefabricstore.com/collections/wool/products/glen-plaid-deadstock-suiting-khaki-turquoise-burgundy)_

Another one of my favourite features.... rather than adding belt loops, we created an adjustable waist tie that is sewn into the front pleat and back dart. If you make the right size, it's mostly an interesting design detail, but I do like that it gives you the option to adjust the fit if your body changes - we're stocking a [slider buckle](https://corefabricstore.com/collections/fabrics-for-mitchell-trousers/products/slider-buckle-pair) specifically for this, but you can also use [D-Rings](https://corefabricstore.com/products/d-rings-for-sienna-maker-jacket). You can also play around with front closures, whether you want a [traditional button(opens in new tab)](https://corefabricstore.com/collections/buttons/products/recycled-paper-25mm-1-buttons-2-pack), jeans button, or an ["invisible" sew-on hook and eye](https://corefabricstore.com/products/sew-on-wide-hook-eye-closures) for a sleek finish.

We also added optional back welt pockets (this is a trouser after all!) but you're welcome to skip them or sub them for a back patch pocket as well. We based the front crotch curve of the [Mitchell Trousers](https://closetcorepatterns.com/products/mitchell-trousers-pattern) on our [Pietra Pants](https://closetcorepatterns.com/collections/sewing-patterns-all/products/pietra-pants-shorts-pattern?variant=39419178483846), so if you've made that pattern before you'll know what to expect in terms of crotch fit.

![](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com//wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Mitchell-Trousers-Pattern_Pants-Pattern-2.jpg)![](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com//wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Mitchell-Trousers-Pattern_Technical-Flat.jpg)

If you're wondering what options you have for fabric, the answer is...  a lot! We'll be sharing more specific fabric suggestions in an upcoming post, but in brief, you can use just about any midweight woven for these babies, from structured cottons to denim, wool, and linen. I am also excited to see how they look in a midweight drapey fabric like Tencel.

Difficulty-wise, we have rated this pattern as intermediate, although I think any confident beginner would be in good hands.  We use a modified version of our typical fly front instructions, and if you want to skip the welts it makes this considerably easier and faster to sew. I think you'll really enjoy the novel construction of our front pleated pockets - it's really satisfying to watch them come together!

This pattern is available in PDF (sizes 0-32) and print (0-20). Please note that due to a huge increase in material costs, the print pattern is $22 USD instead of our typical $20. We're hoping prices will come down in the coming year, but due to supply chain issues, we had to switch printers for the pattern tissue and could not avoid a price increase for this pattern. The PDF pattern has not increased in cost.

Finally, if you're wondering who Mitchell is, it won't surprise longtime readers to know we named this pattern after one of my all-time personal heroes, Joni Mitchell. Joni means more to me than I can say; she provided the soundtrack to my childhood and was the glue that held my mom and me together during the worst of my moody teenage years (she would wake me up every Saturday blaring Blue, knowing I couldn't say no to cleaning the house while it was playing), and into my adulthood has provided countless moments of solace, reflection, and inspiration. She also has _incredible_ personal style that leaned more and more to menswear-inspired looks as she got older, and I think she would love these trousers if I could somehow make a pair for her... she's a constant reminder to me that charting your own unique and singular course through life is the greatest journey there is. We hope that while you're wearing your Mitchell Trousers, you'll feel inspired to do the same.

[SHOP MITCHELL(opens in new tab)](https://closetcorepatterns.com/products/mitchell-trousers-pattern)

P.S. A big thank you to Poppy Barley for the oxfords and ankle boots in this shoot! You can get them [here(opens in new tab)](https://poppybarley.com/?gclid=CjwKCAjwyaWZBhBGEiwACslQo1WIntZCskP80myZV73J2CNU3zKPSgOz2cqnF_ocx0pTIjQFzQZktRoCb5sQAvD_BwE).

1. Why is the sizing different for a size 16 (for example) if using the 0-20 range pattern rather than the 14-32 range pattern?





[Reply](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com/introducing-the-mitchell-trousers/#comment-18025)

   - Hi! They are drafted with a different block. The 14-32 range is drafted for a curvier figure (more hips) so use your waist to hip ratio to choose which works for you. Bigger difference= more curves, less difference= 0-20. Hope this helps!

7. I really love the look of the fabric, yellow textured cotton, but it does not seem to be available. Which fabric would you suggest to achieve similar texture/look? What are the terms to search for this kind of fabric? Thanks!





[Reply](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com/introducing-the-mitchell-trousers/#comment-19237)

   - You can find the ‘Perfect match’ fabric selection from Core Fabrics here: [https://corefabricstore.com/collections/fabrics-for-mitchell-trousers](https://corefabricstore.com/collections/fabrics-for-mitchell-trousers)


     If you search ‘Textured cotton fabric for pants’ on your browser, you should find what you are looking for 🙂





     [Reply](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com/introducing-the-mitchell-trousers/#comment-19260)

   - Since the beauty of seersucker is it’s texture, I would not use fusible interfacing. Depending on the type of structured look you want, I would use light to medium weight woven sewn on interfacing or even lightweight muslin.. Adding a cotton interlining to sew the interfacing on would make it easier.


     Make sure to wash your fabric before cutting, the seersucker can shrink a lot.


     Cut your seersucker and cotton interlining with the same pattern pieces.


     Sew your interfacing to your cotton interlining (follow the instruction as the interlining was your top fabric).


     Pin your fabric to your interlining wrong sides together and sew the perimeter of each pieces just inside of the seam allowance.


     Construct the jacket following the instructions. When you press your seams and hems, make sure to use a lot of steam but don\`t press to much or you will flatten the texture. What I like to do is to use the palm of my hand after I steam.





     [Reply](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com/introducing-the-mitchell-trousers/#comment-19264)
8. I have lusted after the Mitchell pattern for ages and finally got it for Christmas! I’m normally a size 13 waist and 12 hips, and the size 14 muslin I’ve made could do with being slightly tighter; the waist is fine. What’s the best way to adjust the hips please?





[Reply](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com/introducing-the-mitchell-trousers/#comment-19252)

   - I always like to do this kind of adjustments by wearing the garment inside out, and pinning from the sides.





     [Reply](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com/introducing-the-mitchell-trousers/#comment-19258)

21 Sep 2022 • [Mitchell Trousers](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com/category/our-patterns/mitchell-trousers/) • by [Heather Lou](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com//author/closetcasefilesgmail-com)

# Introducing the Mitchell Trousers!

![Mitchell-Trousers-Pattern_Pants-Pattern-5](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Mitchell-Trousers-Pattern_Pants-Pattern-5.jpg)

After consecutive [lingerie(opens in new tab)](https://closetcorepatterns.com/collections/sewing-patterns-all/products/chez-moi-collection-bundle?variant=39712032686214) and [swim(opens in new tab)](https://closetcorepatterns.com/collections/sewing-patterns-all/products/faye-swimsuit-pattern?variant=39778960965766) pattern launches this year, it feels SO GOOD to finally introduce some new woven clothing patterns back into the CCP family! We couldn't be happier to add the [Mitchell Trousers](https://closetcorepatterns.com/products/mitchell-trousers-pattern) to our roster, destined to be a wardrobe staple for you this fall and beyond.

Mitchell is our take on a classic pleated trouser. These are too perennial to ever \*really\* go out of style, but if you follow fashion, you've surely noticed trousers are back in a very big way (no doubt a reaction to all the sweats we've been wearing the last few years!) Last fall I was desperate for an alternative to elastic waist pants, so we developed Mitchell to scratch that particular itch. I'm a bit obsessed with the final design - they look super sophisticated and pulled together while also being very comfortable to wear all day long.

![](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com//wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Mitchell-Trousers-Pattern_Plus-Size-Pants-Pattern-09.jpg)![](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com//wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Mitchell-Trousers-Pattern_Pants-Pattern-3.jpg)

[Mitchell](https://closetcorepatterns.com/products/mitchell-trousers-pattern) is a unique trouser pattern in that it doesn't have a waistband. High-waisted and designed to sit at your natural waist, you get a sleek, continuous line throughout the rise. The waist itself is stabilized with an inner facing, so it has all the structure of a waistband without the discomfort of one digging into your middle. We also wanted to avoid the volume around the midsection that can result from too many pleats, so instead, we have one deep pleat that provides sitting ease and comfort while also looking rather architectural and cool as it integrates into the front angled pocket. The pleat is anchored for the first few inches, so again, you don't get that tummy volume you might be used to from traditional pleated pants.

[SHOP MITCHELL(opens in new tab)](https://closetcorepatterns.com/products/mitchell-trousers-pattern)

![](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com//wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Mitchell-Trousers-Pattern_Pants-Pattern-8.jpg)

We love giving you bang for your buck, so we drafted two different major variations for this pattern: a wide leg with a floor-skimming deep hem, and a tapered, slightly cropped leg. This gives you lots of styling and shoe options, whether you want to wear them long with a heel, or cropped and tapered with an oxford, flat, or sneaker.

![](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com//wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Mitchell-Trousers-Pattern_Pants-Pattern-7.jpg)![](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com//wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Mitchell-Trousers-Pattern_Pants-Pattern-9.jpg)![](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com//wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Mitchell-Trousers-Pattern_Plus-Size-Pants-Pattern-01.jpg)![](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com//wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Mitchell-Trousers-Pattern_Plus-Size-Pants-Pattern-04.jpg)![](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com//wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Mitchell-Trousers-Pattern_Plus-Size-Pants-Pattern-06.jpg)![](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com//wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Mitchell-Trousers-Pattern_Plus-Size-Pants-Pattern-08.jpg)![](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com//wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Mitchell-Trousers-Pattern_Pants-Pattern-1.jpg)![](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com//wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Mitchell-Trousers-Pattern_Pants-Pattern-4.jpg)

_Fabrics we used: [Cream recycled denim(opens in new tab)](https://corefabricstore.com/collections/bottomweight/products/upcycled-midweight-10-5-oz-denim-cream), [lightweight denim(opens in new tab)](https://corefabricstore.com/collections/denim-twill/products/6-75-oz-non-stretch-denim-shirting-slate-blue), [yellow textured cotton(opens in new tab)](https://corefabricstore.com/collections/bottomweight/products/textured-non-stretch-cotton-honey), [deadstock wool. (opens in new tab)](https://corefabricstore.com/collections/wool/products/glen-plaid-deadstock-suiting-khaki-turquoise-burgundy)_

Another one of my favourite features.... rather than adding belt loops, we created an adjustable waist tie that is sewn into the front pleat and back dart. If you make the right size, it's mostly an interesting design detail, but I do like that it gives you the option to adjust the fit if your body changes - we're stocking a [slider buckle](https://corefabricstore.com/collections/fabrics-for-mitchell-trousers/products/slider-buckle-pair) specifically for this, but you can also use [D-Rings](https://corefabricstore.com/products/d-rings-for-sienna-maker-jacket). You can also play around with front closures, whether you want a [traditional button(opens in new tab)](https://corefabricstore.com/collections/buttons/products/recycled-paper-25mm-1-buttons-2-pack), jeans button, or an ["invisible" sew-on hook and eye](https://corefabricstore.com/products/sew-on-wide-hook-eye-closures) for a sleek finish.

We also added optional back welt pockets (this is a trouser after all!) but you're welcome to skip them or sub them for a back patch pocket as well. We based the front crotch curve of the [Mitchell Trousers](https://closetcorepatterns.com/products/mitchell-trousers-pattern) on our [Pietra Pants](https://closetcorepatterns.com/collections/sewing-patterns-all/products/pietra-pants-shorts-pattern?variant=39419178483846), so if you've made that pattern before you'll know what to expect in terms of crotch fit.

![](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com//wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Mitchell-Trousers-Pattern_Pants-Pattern-2.jpg)![](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com//wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Mitchell-Trousers-Pattern_Technical-Flat.jpg)

If you're wondering what options you have for fabric, the answer is...  a lot! We'll be sharing more specific fabric suggestions in an upcoming post, but in brief, you can use just about any midweight woven for these babies, from structured cottons to denim, wool, and linen. I am also excited to see how they look in a midweight drapey fabric like Tencel.

Difficulty-wise, we have rated this pattern as intermediate, although I think any confident beginner would be in good hands.  We use a modified version of our typical fly front instructions, and if you want to skip the welts it makes this considerably easier and faster to sew. I think you'll really enjoy the novel construction of our front pleated pockets - it's really satisfying to watch them come together!

This pattern is available in PDF (sizes 0-32) and print (0-20). Please note that due to a huge increase in material costs, the print pattern is $22 USD instead of our typical $20. We're hoping prices will come down in the coming year, but due to supply chain issues, we had to switch printers for the pattern tissue and could not avoid a price increase for this pattern. The PDF pattern has not increased in cost.

Finally, if you're wondering who Mitchell is, it won't surprise longtime readers to know we named this pattern after one of my all-time personal heroes, Joni Mitchell. Joni means more to me than I can say; she provided the soundtrack to my childhood and was the glue that held my mom and me together during the worst of my moody teenage years (she would wake me up every Saturday blaring Blue, knowing I couldn't say no to cleaning the house while it was playing), and into my adulthood has provided countless moments of solace, reflection, and inspiration. She also has _incredible_ personal style that leaned more and more to menswear-inspired looks as she got older, and I think she would love these trousers if I could somehow make a pair for her... she's a constant reminder to me that charting your own unique and singular course through life is the greatest journey there is. We hope that while you're wearing your Mitchell Trousers, you'll feel inspired to do the same.

[SHOP MITCHELL(opens in new tab)](https://closetcorepatterns.com/products/mitchell-trousers-pattern)

P.S. A big thank you to Poppy Barley for the oxfords and ankle boots in this shoot! You can get them [here(opens in new tab)](https://poppybarley.com/?gclid=CjwKCAjwyaWZBhBGEiwACslQo1WIntZCskP80myZV73J2CNU3zKPSgOz2cqnF_ocx0pTIjQFzQZktRoCb5sQAvD_BwE).

1. Why is the sizing different for a size 16 (for example) if using the 0-20 range pattern rather than the 14-32 range pattern?





[Reply](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com/introducing-the-mitchell-trousers/#comment-18025)

   - Hi! They are drafted with a different block. The 14-32 range is drafted for a curvier figure (more hips) so use your waist to hip ratio to choose which works for you. Bigger difference= more curves, less difference= 0-20. Hope this helps!

6. do you think a stretch woven fabric would work for this pattern? Thanks!

7. I really love the look of the fabric, yellow textured cotton, but it does not seem to be available. Which fabric would you suggest to achieve similar texture/look? What are the terms to search for this kind of fabric? Thanks!





[Reply](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com/introducing-the-mitchell-trousers/#comment-19237)

   - You can find the ‘Perfect match’ fabric selection from Core Fabrics here: [https://corefabricstore.com/collections/fabrics-for-mitchell-trousers](https://corefabricstore.com/collections/fabrics-for-mitchell-trousers)


     If you search ‘Textured cotton fabric for pants’ on your browser, you should find what you are looking for 🙂





     [Reply](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com/introducing-the-mitchell-trousers/#comment-19260)

   - Since the beauty of seersucker is it’s texture, I would not use fusible interfacing. Depending on the type of structured look you want, I would use light to medium weight woven sewn on interfacing or even lightweight muslin.. Adding a cotton interlining to sew the interfacing on would make it easier.


     Make sure to wash your fabric before cutting, the seersucker can shrink a lot.


     Cut your seersucker and cotton interlining with the same pattern pieces.


     Sew your interfacing to your cotton interlining (follow the instruction as the interlining was your top fabric).


     Pin your fabric to your interlining wrong sides together and sew the perimeter of each pieces just inside of the seam allowance.


     Construct the jacket following the instructions. When you press your seams and hems, make sure to use a lot of steam but don\`t press to much or you will flatten the texture. What I like to do is to use the palm of my hand after I steam.





     [Reply](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com/introducing-the-mitchell-trousers/#comment-19264)

[Reply](https://blog.closetcorepatterns.com/introducing-the-mitchell-trousers/#comment-19252)
